chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Faddal, from Safwan, from Abu al-Mu'za, from Ibrahim ibn Maymun, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"When the girl is between her parents, she has no authority alongside her parents; and when she has married, she is not married off except with her consent."
ai.seo_question: What is the difference in marriage authority between a minor girl and a married/adult girl in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the transition of marital authority, establishing that while parents retain guardianship over a minor daughter, an adult woman possesses the right of *rida* (consent) to validate her marriage contract. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that consent is a fundamental pillar of the marriage contract, distinguishing between the legal capacity of the guardian and the personal agency of the bride. It serves as a key evidence for the validity of the woman contracting her own marriage (*nikah al-nafs*) once she reaches maturity.
